tip: искала then нашла (iskala, nashla): the imperfective describes the process of searching, and the perfective marks the successful result of finding.
решал then решил (reshal, reshil): the imperfective form shows the hour-long effort, and the perfective form marks the moment it finally got solved.
To say about X, use о (o = about) plus the noun in -е (-e): о физике (o fizike = about physics). Before a vowel it becomes об (ob), as in об отце (ob attse = about dad).
Weather questions use какая (kakaya = what kind), agreeing with feminine погода (pagoda = weather), where English just says how.
обычно (abychna = usually) takes the imperfective писали (pisali = wrote), stressing a repeated habit, not one finished paper.
сразу (srazu = at once) marks a finished action, so the perfective написал (napisal = wrote) is used, not the process form писал (pisal).
наконец (nakanets = finally) points to a result, so the perfective сделали (sdelali = did) is used, not the ongoing делали (delali).
Past verbs agree with the subject's gender: feminine она (ana) takes строила (stroila = built) with -ла, while a man would say строил (stroil).
отвечать (atvechat = to answer) pairs with на (na) plus the accusative: отвечала на письмо (atvechala na pismo = answered the letter).
забыть (zabyt = to forget) takes о (o) about something, which becomes об (ob) before a vowel: забыла об этом (zabyla ob etam = forgot about it).
Leaving a person uses от (ot = from) plus the genitive: ушла от подруги (ushla ot padrugi = left her friend).
Cold has no subject here: холодно (kholadna = cold) is an adverb form used for weather and how a place feels.
Needing something puts the person in the dative: мне (mne = to me) plus понадобится (panadobitsya = will be needed), literally to-me it will be needed.
весь день (ves den = all day) describes duration, so the imperfective писал (pisal = was writing) is used, not the finished написал (napisal).
чтобы (chtoby = in order to) plus an infinitive shows purpose: чтобы понять (chtoby panyat = in order to understand).
Repeated round trips use the multidirectional ходила (khadila = went), not the one-way шла (shla), so часто ходила (chasta khadila) means going there again and again.
After numbers from five up, the noun usually goes to genitive plural: пятнадцать минут (pyatnadtsat minut = fifteen minutes), not минуты (minuty).
Going to a person uses к (k = to) plus the dative: к врачу (k vrachu = to the doctor), where places take в (v) or на (na).
The receiver of дал (dal = gave) stands in the dative: своему брату (svayemu bratu = to my brother).
Playing a game uses играть (igrat) plus в (v) and the accusative: играет в шахматы (igrayet v shakhmaty = plays chess).
каждое утро (kazhdaye utra = every morning) signals a habit, so the multidirectional плавали (plavali = swam) fits regular swims.
бегали (begali = ran around) is the multidirectional form for running in all directions, not toward one goal like бегут (begut).
сколько бы он ни (skolka by on ni = no matter how much) makes a concession: however much he works, it is never enough.
Unreal past uses если бы (esli by = if) with a past verb, then бы again: мы бы не опоздали (my by ne apazdali = we would not have been late).
A perfective in present form means future: помоет (pamoyet = will wash) refers to tomorrow, with no separate will word.
помогать (pamagat = to help) governs the dative, not the accusative: помогает другу (pamagayet drugu = helps a friend).
Repeated losing uses the imperfective терял (teryal = lost): постоянно терял (pastayanna teryal) marks it happening over and over.
A single completed loss uses the perfective потерял (pateryal = lost), formed by adding по- to терял (teryal).
Motion toward one goal uses the unidirectional бегут (begut = are running): бегут на площадку (begut na plashchadku = running to the playground) means heading there now.
лучший (luchshiy = best) is the irregular superlative of good, standing in for a regular form like самый хороший (samyy kharoshiy).
